thread:
jessica_support: Hi team — Customer (CareBridge / Dr. Patel) just opened an urgent request: they need a 90-day export of access/audit logs for an upcoming HIPAA review. They say the export endpoint returns 403. Ticket #CS-48291.

dr_rahul_patel: Thanks, this is high priority. Their legal needs logs for 2025-01-01 to 2025-03-31. We signed the healthcare addendum last year. Can you confirm retention window and export permissions?

jessica_support: Confirmed they have BAA + healthcare addendum on file (contract id HB-2024-77). I tried the export from our console as the account admin and hit a 403 with this payload: 

```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/exports" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  -d '{"start":"2025-01-01","end":"2025-03-31","format":"ndjson","scope":"audit_logs"}'

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"access_denied","message":"KMS key policy prevents cross-project export"}
```

jessica_support: I also tried from the customer org (scoped token) and got same.

raj_security: Noted. Two possibilities: 1) export service attempts to wrap the archive with a KMS key that is scoped to our infra project; key policy may not include the customer's service account OR 2) an export-safety ACL that blocks exports for healthcare addendum customers to force manual review. I'll check KMS key policy. @marco_sre can you repro with a service-account token?

marco_sre: Repro steps I used: 
1) impersonate service account `svc-exporter@redwood-prod`
2) hit /v1/exports with same body
3) observe 403 + `kms:Encrypt` denied in logs.

Log snippet: `ERROR export_service: Encrypt failed: user="svc-exporter@redwood-prod" resource="projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/hipaa/cryptoKeys/ehr-exports": PermissionDenied`

marco_sre: So it looks like the key `ehr-exports` policy doesn't include the `svc-exporter` principal. Strange because infra changes in Nov included that key.

lina_acctexec: CareBridge is asking for a confirmed timeline. Audit starts next Tues. They expect the export completed before audit kickoff. Customer is escalating to their compliance team.

jessica_support: I've attached the ticket with customer screenshots: https://redwood.cust.link/tickets/CS-48291 (internal). They also pasted a redacted error from their UI which matches the curl output.

raj_security: I'm creating an internal escalation to security-ops and key-owners. Action plan: 
- (A) verify key policy for `projects/redwood-prod/.../ehr-exports` and add `serviceAccount:svc-exporter@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` if missing.
- (B) check if export flow for healthcare-addendum accounts has an explicit manual-approval gate; if so, trigger approval and record the exception.
- (C) if the key is customer-owned (KMS/HSM), coordinate with customer for key access.

jessica_support: Quick note from customer: they said they uploaded a customer-managed key last quarter for on-prem redaction. So possibility (C) is real. Dr. Patel, did you register a CMEK for exports?

dr_rahul_patel: We did provision a customer-managed key via our KMS provider and shared key metadata with Redwood support. We were told it was attached to exports. We do not have direct HSM access.

raj_security: Ok — we need to confirm whether the export flow honors CMEK for historical audit-log archives or only for live model artifacts. If the customer's CMEK is expected to wrap the archive, the key policy must allow `cryptoKeyVersions` use by our export service principal.

marco_sre: I've opened a temporary infra patch to allow `svc-exporter` to use the key and tested a dry-run export. Dry-run succeeded (archive created, not yet uploaded): `status: ready (encrypted)` 

marco_sre: After the patch I retried the curl and got 200, archive token returned. I then revoked the temporary grant.

raj_security: Good repro. Next steps: 
- Add permanent least-privileged binding for export service on `ehr-exports` key OR implement an export-permissions-check that surfaces a clear admin-facing error (currently it's opaque 403).
- If customer-supplied key was misconfigured, we need a short playbook to walk customers through granting `cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to `svc-exporter` and optionally to a customer-managed service account.

jessica_support: Action items for me: update ticket CS-48291 with timeline and ask customer to confirm whether they want Redwood to provision the grant or they will handle it. Also ask for CMS of their KMS key ARN.

lina_acctexec: I'll prepare an email template for the customer with two options (we apply the binding with their written ACK, or they provide the corrected IAM grant).

compliance-bot: NOTE: For customers under healthcare addendum, all KMS policy changes must be logged and retained for 7 years. Make sure to attach the policy-change audit to the ticket. :locked_with_key: 

jessica_support: Thanks. I'll wait for customer ACK. If no response in 4 hours we escalate to oncall.

dr_rahul_patel: ACK. Please proceed to apply the grant — we authorize Redwood to make the minimum change required and to attach the audit record to the ticket.

jessica_support: Applying the change now (will follow up with final export link). :white_check_mark: 

marco_sre: Export completed and uploaded to the customer's S3 bucket. Shared link (internal): https://storage.redwood.internal/exports/carebridge/CS-48291/20250301-archive.ndjson.gpg

jessica_support: Closing loop — emailed Dr. Patel the secure download and attached the key-policy audit. Marking ticket as pending customer confirmation.

dr_rahul_patel: Received, downloading now. Thank you all for the quick turnaround.

jessica_support: Filed follow-up to improve the error message and to add explicit guidance to the healthcare addendum onboarding docs for CMEK exports.

raj_security: I'll own the post-mortem and add a short runbook for support.

jessica_support: End of thread.
